title: What should you ask first in a pricing case, and which trap should you avoid?
description: The first question to ask in a pricing case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Pricing cases have no single right answer, which can feel unsettling. Here is how to reach a sensible number and defend it.
body:
The first question to ask

What is the product worth to the customer?

How to build your structure

  • Floor: variable cost per unit, fixed costs to recover
  • Ceiling: value to the customer, price of their next best option
  • Reference: competitor prices, substitutes
  • Choose: penetration or skimming, volume at each price, effect on our other products

The trap most people fall into

Using only one lens; no volume assumption.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the pricing framework.

Two prompts to try

What price should a company charge for fast EV charging?

Show a model structure
  • Cost floor: Electricity, grid fees, equipment per kWh; Utilisation needed to break even
  • Customer value: Cost of charging at home vs on the road; Time saved, convenience
  • Competitors: Rivals' prices, subscriptions; Fuel cost per mile as a reference
  • Structure: Per kWh, per minute, subscription; Peak and off-peak

Where to start: Cost floor vs value ceiling: price sits between the two.

The trap: Copying rivals' prices without knowing your own cost and utilisation.

Should an electronics retailer introduce a price-match guarantee?

Show a model structure
  • Customer impact: Extra sales from confidence; Share of customers who would claim
  • Cost: Margin given up on matched sales; Admin to check claims
  • Competitor response: Rivals matching back, price war; Online-only rivals
  • Rules: Which rivals and products; In-store vs online

Where to start: Cost: how many sales would be matched, and at what discount.

The trap: Assuming only a few customers will claim.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
